why_null: Every case in the library was considered against the motif of mbg-jobs, which is an input count carried as an output measure: a workforce figure produced by multiplying a per-kitchen staffing assumption by a kitchen count, sourced to the body that runs the programme, then set up as the measure of the programme's worth with no cost denominator beside it, no account of what the counted heads were doing beforehand, and no offsetting count for the vendors whose daily sales the free portion lands in place of. B-01, the casualty-inflation cascade, runs on a count whose circulation outran its verification and whose force came from moral shock; the mbg-jobs count has a stated derivation, and the gap sits in what it is never set against rather than in how it travelled. B-02, the provision cascade, turns on provisions attributed to a bill whose final text was not yet public, which is a claim about the content of a rule; the mbg-jobs chain makes no claim about the text of any rule. B-03, moral-shock acceleration, is a timing shape, a single image compressing mobilization into hours; this family moves administrative figures across months, with no shock and no acceleration in it. B-04, the scope-inflation panic, is the nearest thing in the library and still short of the threshold: its shape is an instrument narrowed in law and widened in the telling, a restricted scope priced as though it reached the whole consumption basket. Nothing in mbg-jobs is narrowed by an instrument and widened in the retelling; stated coverage and reported coverage agree, and the unstated step is the comparison the count is never placed beside. A shared subject of counting is not a shared motif, and sector, institution and period sit outside the test by blueprint. No documented episode in the library carries the shape of a self-sourced input count standing where a net measure belongs, so this narrative takes silence.
